item.title: Brits would quite like their private messages to stay private
item.description:
📝 A third said the government shouldn't have that power at all, while another 41 percent wanted greater transparency or parliamentary oversight. 84 percent worried that mechanisms allowing access to encrypted messages could introduce vulnerabilities for hackers and criminals, while 82 percent were concerned the powers could be abused. 65 percent said they'd become more cautious about what they liked, shared or commented on, while 41 percent said they'd self-censor criticism of public institutions or government officials.
🔗 Read more: https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/08/30/turns-out-brits-would-quite-like-their-private-messages-to-stay-private/5292994

item.title: Fair Work Commission condemns 'plain wrong' AI legal advice
item.description:
📝 (Reuters: Dado Ruvic)In short:A former ALDI worker seeking to challenge his dismissal in the Fair Work Commission has been criticised for bringing a doomed case that was informed by AI. From October 20, applicants to the Fair Work Commission will need to disclose AI use, while a template to help AI-dependent litigants has been implemented. "A sacked ALDI employee challenged his dismissal in the Fair Work Commission.
